messages.subject: read.genalex and aboot functions, how to change labels?
messages.subject_clean: read.genalex and aboot functions, how to change labels?
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I am trying to show the species names in the final dendrogram I get from the aboot function. I have the data in genalex format and I understand I cannot have my samples labeled as alpha characters, instead I should use alpha numeric characters in genalex. That's ok but how can I replace them by the actual species/cultivar names in the final dendrogram?

Any help is much appreciated.

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] read.genalex and aboot functions, how to change labels?
messages.subject_clean: [poppr] read.genalex and aboot functions, how to change labels?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jose,

There's no reason why you can't have your samples labeled with the species/cultivar names in your GenAlEx file. You can name them there. Otherwise, if you already named them with numbers, you can set the sample names in your data set with:

indNames(dat) <- vector_of_names # assuming you have a vector of names

You can plot the output of aboot using the plot.phylo function from ape for further customization.

Best,
Zhian

-----
Zhian N. Kamvar, Ph. D.
Postdoctoral Researcher (Everhart Lab)
Department of Plant Pathology
University of Nebraska-Lincoln

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] read.genalex and aboot functions, how to change labels?
messages.subject_clean: [poppr] read.genalex and aboot functions, how to change labels?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jose,

indNames() comes from the adegenet package (poppr uses much of the functionality from adegenet in the underlying code). It allows you to replace the sample names in your data set with anything you want. You can find the details in section 3.3 of the "basics" tutorial for adegenet: (https://github.com/thibautjombart/adegenet/wiki/Tutorials).

So if you had a spreadsheet of sample names, you could read it in and replace your numeric names with those.

That being said, your problem may be how your spreadsheet program converts data to CSV or there may be a hidden newline character in your data. Either way, you can also try to use the read.genalexcel() function from the popprxl package on your XLS data.

Hope that helps,
Zhian

-----
Zhian N. Kamvar, Ph. D.
Postdoctoral Researcher (Everhart Lab)
Department of Plant Pathology
University of Nebraska-Lincoln

messages.subject_clean: [poppr] read.genalex and aboot functions, how to change labels?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jose,

indNames() expects a character vector but you gave it a data frame. You need to tell R which column you want to use as the individual names. When you read in a csv file, it gets read into R as a data frame. So, if your individual names are located in column 2 of your file, you should use:

indNames(mydata) <- list[[2]]

If you need a refresher in R, I would recommend following the examples here: https://everhartlab.github.io/IntroR/Part1-Introduction.html or using the interactive tutorial package, swirl (http://swirlstats.com/).

Hope that helps,
Zhian

-----
Zhian N. Kamvar, Ph. D.
Postdoctoral Researcher (Everhart Lab)
Department of Plant Pathology

messages.subject: Error in read.genalex when geo = TRUE
messages.subject_clean: Error in read.genalex when geo = TRUE
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to import my genalex formatted .csv file using read.genalex.
Something is wrong with my geographical coordinates, because if I remove my coordinates from the .csv and set geo = FALSE, the file imports.
Please advise where I'm going wrong, Ive tried everything I can think of!

Kindest regards.

locixy <- read.genalex("D:/Dropbox/_PhD/r/locixy.csv", ploidy = 2, geo = TRUE)
Error in read.genalex("D:/Dropbox/_PhD/r/locixy.csv", ploidy = 2, geo = TRUE) :
  Something went wrong. Please ensure that your data is formatted correctly:

 Is the ploidy flag set to the maximum ploidy of your data?
 You set geo = TRUE. Do you have geographic coordinates in the right place?
 If you have regional data: did you set the flag?

 Otherwise, the problem may lie within the data structure itself.
  - Inspect your data; if it looks fine then
  - search the poppr forum for the error message; if you still can't find a solution:
    1. Make a minimum working example of your error (see http://stackoverflow.com/a/5963610)
    2. Use the 'reprex' package to reproduce the error (see https://github.com/jennybc/reprex#readme)
    3. Create a new issue on https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/issues

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Error in read.genalex when geo = TRUE
messages.subject_clean: [poppr] Error in read.genalex when geo = TRUE
messages.body_plain:
Hi David,

The issue turns out to be minor. Replace the 1 in the first row of your CSV with a 0.

The reason for that is because poppr will check to make sure that the number of populations you defined in the first row of the header match the number of populations recorded in the second row. It's a wonky artifact of the way the genalex format works.

Hope that helps,
Zhian

-----
Zhian N. Kamvar, Ph. D.
Postdoctoral Researcher (Everhart Lab)
Department of Plant Pathology
University of Nebraska-Lincoln
ORCID: 0000-0003-1458-7108

> The issue turns out to be minor. Replace the 1 in the first row of your CSV with a 0.
>
> The reason for that is because poppr will check to make sure that the number of populations you defined in the first row of the header match the number of populations recorded in the second row. It's a wonky artifact of the way the genalex format works.
>
> Hope that helps,
